TestSchema::test_drop_column_compact.description: Single node: creates a WITH COMPACT STORAGE table (enabled via cluster_options enable_create_table_with_compact_storage) and asserts ALTER TABLE ... DROP c1 raises InvalidRequest matching 'Cannot drop columns from a' (assert_invalid -> _assert_exception tools/assertions.py:60, re.search). Guards the non-CQL3 drop-column validation (CASSANDRA-3919 era).

TestSchema::test_drop_column_compact.relevance: Live: cql3/statements/alter_table_statement.cc:410-411 throws 'Cannot drop columns from a non-CQL3 table'. But COMPACT STORAGE is deprecated, gated by enable_create_table_with_compact_storage (db/config.cc:1752, default false, 'will eventually be removed').
TestSchema::test_drop_column_compact.reason: No scylla test found asserting the non-CQL3 DROP rejection (grep 'Cannot drop columns' in test/ empty), so coverage is unique, but it is a trivial single-node CQL validation of a deprecated feature (db/config.cc:1752) better placed in cqlpy (e.g. test/cqlpy/test_guardrail_compact_storage.py). Note: class marks single_node/next_gating; 5s, 100% pass.

TestSchema::test_drop_column_compaction.description: Single node, server-side timestamps: insert 3 rows, ALTER TABLE DROP c1, ADD c1 int, insert 1 more row, flush+compact, reconnect and assert SELECT c1 returns [None,None,None,4] (assert_all, ignore_order, tools/assertions.py:193 '=='). Originally (CASSANDRA-3919) it also erased dropped_columns from system.schema_columnfamilies and restarted, to prove compaction physically purged the dropped data.

commits.d31b560756: REMOVED the 'erase dropped_columns + restart' step (CASSANDRA-6717 schema tables), so the 'compacted away' check no longer verifies purging.
commits.2bb3eef00c: pre-origin (drop_column_test, renamed/split into this test in 5ea6bd85ca).
commits.26d097cd9f: prepare(): takes cluster_topology dict (default 1 node) instead of nodes_num; rf default 1 (affects all tests via prepare).
commits.53ff2b634a: prepare(): session.use_client_timestamp=False (server-side timestamps, needed for drop+re-add).

TestSchema::test_restart_with_large_tabl.description: Reproducer for scylladb#2623 (boot hang): sets max_cached_partition_size_in_kb=1, creates 100 tables each with a 1KB column name (large system schema partitions), restarts the node and runs SELECTs on first/last table. Only asserts the node boots and queries don't error. The hang was a deadlock in row_cache when a partition exceeded max_cached_partition_size_in_kb and a second sstable reader was created under the read-concurrency semaphore (fix 0ac2c388b6, branch-1.7).

origin.summary: Tomasz Grabiec: 'Add reproducer for hang during boot with large schemas' (mailing-list patch).

The option is now an unknown yaml key (utils/config_file.cc:307 'Unknown option').

TestSchema::test_alter_keyspace_then_tab.description: 2 nodes (2 racks, 1 DC): create keyspace RF=1, UDT ks.my_type, table cf with a UDT column (STCS), ALTER KEYSPACE to RF=2 (or rack list ['rack1','rack2'] when RF is auto-expanded), then ALTER TABLE compaction to LCS. Passes if no 'Unknown type ks.my_type' error. Reproducer for scylla-enterprise#2989 / scylladb#14139 (ALTER KEYSPACE dropped in-memory UDT metadata, fixed by scylla 1a521172ec).
